forms.name: bench-matrix
forms.question: How do these models compare across many benchmarks at once?
forms.whenToUse: Comparing a handful of models across many named benchmarks in one glance, especially when one model is the protagonist.
forms.antiUse: Trends over time or more than ~6 models — use a time-series form or a ranking board instead of a wide table.
forms.props: models (id, label, vendor?, color?, hero? — hero color must be a 6-digit hex, tint is built by hex+alpha concat), groups (label + rows {bench, note?, values: (number|null)[], decimals?}), meta?, footnote?, decimals?=1, benchColLabel?='benchmark'

forms.name: bubble-field
forms.question: How do entities spread across two count dimensions, and which are the heavyweights?
forms.whenToUse: Positioning a dozen-odd named entities on two count metrics that span several orders of magnitude, with a third count as bubble size.
forms.antiUse: Log-log count data spanning decades only — not linear data; skip it for narrow ranges, negative/zero values, or a single dimension.
forms.props: points: {x, y, size, label, series, color?}[]; xLabel; yLabel; legendUnit? (color defaults to seriesColor by series index)

forms.name: distribution-bar
forms.question: How does the whole split into parts?
forms.whenToUse: One flat categorical breakdown of a total (language mix, task mix, traffic sources) where shares matter more than absolute comparison.
forms.antiUse: Comparing values across multiple groups or over time — use a ranking bar list or time series instead; also avoid with many tiny segments that all fall below the label threshold.
forms.props: segments: { label, value, color? }[] (color falls back to palette by index); unit?: string appended in tooltips

forms.name: dune-flow
forms.question: What made up the flow over time, and when were the waves?
forms.whenToUse: Daily composition of a volume stream (issues by priority, requests by tier) where the trend shape matters more than exact per-day spikes.
forms.antiUse: When readers must read exact values off the chart — the B-spline deliberately does not pass through the data points (raw values live only in the tooltip).
forms.props: days: ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD'[] (min 4); series: { label, color?, values: (number|null)[] }[] stacked bottom-up; yLabel?: string

forms.name: frontier-board
forms.question: Which model delivers the most score per dollar (or token), and at what effort level?
forms.whenToUse: Comparing models on a quality-vs-cost tradeoff when each model has multiple runs (effort levels / modes) that form a frontier.
forms.antiUse: Needs >=2 runs per model to draw frontier lines; single-point-per-model data reads better as rank-bars.
forms.props: title, versions[] (datasets of models with runs), metrics[] (X-axis toggles with tickPrefix/Suffix), yMax/yTickSuffix, subjectId highlight, UI label strings

forms.name: pipeline-flow
forms.question: What are the stages of this process, and in what order does work flow?
forms.whenToUse: Explaining a linear multi-step process (ETL, CI, review pipeline) where order matters more than metrics.
forms.antiUse: Not for branching/looping flows or quantitative comparison between stages — no values are encoded.
forms.props: steps: {name, desc}[] ordered stages; accent?: string arrow color (default seriesColor(0))

forms.name: race-lines
forms.question: Who is pulling ahead over time, and by how much on any given day?
forms.whenToUse: Daily/weekly activity or usage volumes for a handful of competing entities where per-date comparison matters.
forms.antiUse: Few data points (<8), many series (>6, tooltip and lines turn to spaghetti), or when only the latest value matters (use a ranking bar instead).
forms.props: days: ISO date strings; series: { label, values (number|null), color?, legendValue?, highlight? }[]; yLabel?: accessible label

forms.name: radar-profile
forms.question: Where does A beat B, and where does it lose?
forms.whenToUse: Head-to-head profile of two entities across 4-8 comparable dimensions normalized to 0-100 (capability profiles, skill matchups).
forms.antiUse: Exactly 2 entities on a 0-100 scale only — not for 3+ overlapping shapes, unnormalized metrics, or precise value reading (use rank bars or a table).
forms.props: axes: string[]; a/b: {label, values: number[] (0-100 per axis), color? (defaults seriesColor(0)/(1))}

forms.name: rank-bars
forms.question: Who leads this ranking, and by how much?
forms.whenToUse: Comparing one metric across a handful of named entities where order and gaps matter (leaderboards, price ladders).
forms.antiUse: Not for time series, part-to-whole composition, or more than ~10 rows — use a table or sparklines instead.
forms.props: items: {label, value, valueLabel?, sub?, highlight?, color?}[]; maxValue?; unit?; highlightColor? (default seriesColor(0))

forms.name: stacked-activity
forms.question: What makes up each day's volume, and how does it breathe day to day?
forms.whenToUse: Daily volume split into 2-4 additive parts over weeks of data, where per-day composition matters as much as the trend.
forms.antiUse: Comparing exact values of individual segments across days (inner segments have no common baseline) or fewer than 5 days.
forms.props: days: ISO date strings; segments: {key,label,color,values[]} bottom-up; unit?; note?; partialLast?; partialNote?

forms.name: tug-of-war
forms.question: Who wins where, head to head?
forms.whenToUse: Head-to-head comparison of exactly two entities across several arenas (benchmarks, markets, categories) where per-row winner and margin matter.
forms.antiUse: Not for 3+ contenders, absolute magnitudes, or trends over time — the rope only shows the relative split per row.
forms.props: left/right: {label, color?} (defaults seriesColor(0)/(1)); rows: {bench, leftValue, rightValue, date?}[]; footnote?

forms.name: waffle-grid
forms.question: How big is this share of the whole, really?
forms.whenToUse: Making a single percentage feel tangible — one share of one whole, where counting units beats reading a number.
forms.antiUse: Not for comparing several shares, time trends, or non-percentage values — use rank bars or a distribution bar instead.
forms.props: value: number (0-100 cells filled); color? (default seriesColor(0)); caption: string

forms.name: warming-stripes
forms.question: When was this field hot, and when was it cold?
forms.whenToUse: Long multi-decade timelines where the story is alternating hot/cold eras, not exact values.
forms.antiUse: Short ranges or continuous quantitative series — use a line or bar chart when exact magnitudes matter.
forms.props: from/to year range; eras[{start,end,heat 0-3,label?}]; note?; colors? 4-step ramp override
